content.text: The only MFN-style provision in the document runs in our favour, so no redline is needed.

input.quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation running against Client. The sole best-terms provision (Section 6, Documentation and Disputes) is granted by TrueLink in Client's favour: TrueLink's Hosting Services rates may not exceed those charged to any other party, plus a one-year price freeze. I also reviewed Compensation (§5) and Client's covenants and warranties (§8), and searched for "most favored", "no less favorable", "best" and "any other party" language; nothing obliges Client to extend TrueLink terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position (no MFN burdening Customer, vendor-granted MFN welcome), so no redline is proposed.
